title: Holy ground again (Joshua 5:13–15)
hookLine: a captain of the Lord's host tells Joshua to loose his shoe, as Moses once did
carry: stand still, and know where you are

lines: A MAN WITH A DRAWN SWORD.
cards: "Art thou for us, or for our adversaries?" That's Joshua's question, and it's a fair one. He's near Jericho, the walled city his people have to face.
He looks up, and a man is standing in front of him with a drawn sword in his hand. Joshua doesn't run. He walks straight up to him and asks what a general would want to know.
Whose side are you on? The answer is one he didn't ask for, and it changes the question.

teach.b: The stranger's first word, in Hebrew, is lo. No. Not for you, not for your enemies.
I have come as captain of the host of the Lord. Joshua falls on his face and asks what his lord wants of his servant. The reply isn't a battle plan.
It's this: take your shoe off your foot, for "the place whereon thou standest is holy." That sentence has been heard before.

teach.h: AS MOSES DID AT THE BUSH.
teach.b: Moses at the burning bush, the first time God speaks to him: put off thy shoes, "for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground."
Now Moses is gone, and his assistant, at the start of his own hardest days, hears the same words.
The way Moses began, Joshua begins. One small difference: Moses is told to take off his shoes. Joshua is told to take off his shoe, just one.
The text doesn't say why. Then the text does nothing. The captain delivers no message.
The scene ends: and Joshua did so. So what was the visit for? One answer in the Talmud says the captain came because the people had let their Torah study slip in the camp.

Another way to read it is just as it stands: the message was the ground. Before the walls, before strategy, before anyone asks whose side God is on, Joshua is asked to stand still, barefoot, and know where he is.

how: In synagogue, kohanim take off their shoes before they go up to recite the priestly blessing over the congregation.

games.q: you're Joshua, near Jericho. a man with a drawn sword stands in front of you. what do you do?
o: turn back to the camp for help.
walk up and ask whose side he's on.
games.why: Joshua walks straight up to him: "Art thou for us, or for our adversaries?" the answer is no, and then: take off your shoe.

practice: If you can, take off your shoes, or one shoe, and stand; if standing isn't possible, sit with bare feet flat on the floor.
Feel what's under you, wood, tile, carpet, cold or warm, an ordinary floor in an ordinary room, and stand on it as if it mattered. If you pray, this can be your prayer: just standing here.

wordCard.voice: Joshua, told by a stranger with a drawn sword near Jericho to take off one shoe, for the place where he stood was holy, just as Moses once heard at the bush.

orig.note: Hebrew: holy. the last word of the captain's sentence to Joshua.

carryVoice: Your line: stand still, and know where you are. Before the walls came the ground. See you tomorrow.
